correctness.rationale: For irrational alpha>1, the one-step inverse y=floor(x/alpha)+1 exists exactly if u={x/alpha}>1-1/alpha. The second inversion reduces to {v+(1-u)/alpha}>1-1/alpha with v={x/alpha²}. Since the unreduced argument lies in (0,2), its split at 1 gives exactly the stated C_alpha and disjoint E_alpha: 1-1/alpha<u<2-alpha and v>2-2/alpha+u/alpha. The triangular branch exists only if alpha<phi; its Lebesgue area is (1-alpha+1/alpha)^2/(2alpha), equal to natural density under rational independence by Kronecker–Weyl. For alpha=sqrt(2) restricted fractional orbit makes E empty. Direct finite independent decimal membership tests support but do not establish the infinite density.
residual_risks: Finite checks are corroboration only; the analytic proof supplies the quantified claim.
